changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8871-page-node-refuses-breadcrumbs.md`

- names `layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` → `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured, on this branch's base `93127bd6f`.** Zero readers, with a **point-access** probe rather than a bare word: on that base `\.breadcrumbs` scores 0 tree-wide (exit 1) against `\.breadcrumb\b`'s **12** files tree-wide (**10** under `packages/`) as the lit control. At head the same two probes read 16 and 13 and `\.breadcrumbs` is exit 0 over 4 files — every hit one of this branch's own four files (this changeset, the refusal pin, `layout.ts`, `zod/layout.zod.ts`) quoting the probe string, and the pin's own exclusions put head back at exit 1. The base reading is the measurement; the head reading is this branch's echo of it. The bare word would have lied — it also names Sentry's own unrelated concept (`app-shell/src/observability/sentry.ts`) and appears in two comments listing UI surfaces (`core/src/utils/record-title.ts`, `layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx`), so a bare probe reports five readers that do not exist.

### `.changeset/objectchart-fieldoptionlabel-ref-5587.md`

- names `useObjectLabel.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts` — edited by this change

  > Pinned by `ObjectChart.fieldOptionLabelRefetch.test.tsx`, which counts fetches across forced re-renders both outside and inside a provider. Reverting `useObjectLabel.ts` to its pre-objectui#5564 state turns the no-provider case red (2 fetches instead of 1, alongside React's "Maximum update depth exceeded"), so the removal is pinned to the fix that unlocked it rather than to a comment.

### `.changeset/objectpivottable-i18n-resolver-refs-5625.md`

- names `useObjectLabel.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts` — edited by this change

  > Pinned by `ObjectPivotTable.i18nResolverDeps.test.tsx`, which counts derivations across forced re-renders both outside and inside a provider, checks that the two derived state maps settle, and asserts the language-switch re-derivation. Reverting `useObjectLabel.ts` to its pre-objectui#5585 state turns the no-provider case red (derivations in the dozens instead of 1), so the removal is pinned to the fix that unlocked it rather than to a comment.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1563d3e10` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1867 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2479 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36796596370)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `54656bd7df48f550ccb72b912e6f0276f5d04261`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11201 (body and all 12 comments; the director's ruling `5921167691` is the binding direction, claim `5921933038`, dev report `5922299030`), PR #11297 (body, 5-file list, net diff against `main`; the base `1563d3e10b` is `main` at review time), and the head's check-runs with `filter=latest`. Context reads by `contents` at the head or base, not runs: `NavigationRenderer.tsx`, `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx`, layout `package.json`, `types/src/app.ts`, `types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`, `cli/src/commands/validate.ts`, `previews/navItemLabel.ts`, `layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx`, `views/nav-menu-renderer.tsx`, `react/src/index.ts`, the six producer files and `useNavigationSync.ts`; and the spec's `i18n.zod.ts`, `i18n-label-resolver.ts` and `i18n-resolver.ts` from the objectstack checkout (the key lookahead landed 2026-09-21 in `5c5b67fc4`, before the 17.5.0 objectui resolves).

**Check-runs on the head: 43 — 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress** (polled 00:37Z to 00:45Z; the 8 test shards, Type Check, Lint and Spec Main Shape Gate all completed success). The gate verdicts are green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The deletion — right.** `resolveNavItemLabel` is now three lines: separator, the absent arm (`inheritedNavItemLabel`, unchanged) and the present arm (`presentNavItemLabel`). The `isCustomized` closure, its comment and the `(item as any).dashboardName` reads are gone. Every delegate at the head: `inheritedNavItemLabel` keys on absence alone and asks `targetLabel` by target identity; `resolveLabel` compares only an i18next result to its own key; the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` compares locale tags. The one other text comparison in the file is `filterNavigationItems`, label against the search query. The four label reads in the component (group, action, item, search) and the filter's default all route through `resolveNavItemLabel`. No remaining code path compares a label to a name, and nothing added does: `isKeyedLabel` tests member names of the label object, never its text against a target.

2. **The map resolution against the ruling's words — satisfies the ruling as parameterised; the pin's literal "the locale's value" is met only as the resolver's locale default, and that gap is Q1, declared in the title, body, changeset and test header.** (a) The gap the ruling cites (`5913605784`) is "would render empty in the runtime sidebar"; at the head a map renders text through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel`, the same import `AppSchemaRenderer.resolveAreaLabel` and `navItemLabel.ts` use. (b) "The way areas already do": layout's own `resolveAreaLabel` is the same call, `resolveInlineI18nLabel(label, undefined) ?? ''`, with a docblock that names the no-locale default "a floor, not a ceiling" and a host prop as the only sanctioned route to more. But the two other "already do" sites resolve with a locale: `UnifiedSidebar` resolves AREA maps with the viewer's `language` (line 552), and the designer canvas takes a `locale`. `translateApp` does not flatten inline maps (it replaces by `id` only), so a map does reach the renderer, and in the console a zh-CN viewer sees the `en` entry of a map-valued ENTRY label under area labels in zh-CN. (c) Read literally, the ruling requires the viewer's locale inside `resolveNavItemLabel`; its own parameters ("no schema, type or public prop change", Clause-② `no`, level S, patch) exclude the route the package documents (a locale prop from the host), and the exported pure function's other call sites (`CommandPalette`, `SearchResultsPage`, `nav-menu-renderer`, `navItemLabel.ts`) would need a locale argument as well. One route the dev did not name: `@object-ui/react`, a layout dependency, re-exports `useI18nContext` from `@object-ui/i18n`, so a locale is reachable with no prop — at the cost of the coupling `resolveAreaLabel` documents as forbidden, and of a split (sidebar in the viewer's locale, palette and search at `en`) unless the signature changes. That is a design decision for the follow-up card, not for this PR. Judgment: the floor is the ceiling the ruling's parameters allow, so the PR does not fall short of the ruling; the ruling's pin and its parameters disagree with each other, and that disagreement is Q1.

3. **Map versus keyed — a shape test, sound for every map the spec accepts.** `isKeyedLabel` is `'key' in label || 'defaultValue' in label`. The spec's `INLINE_LOCALE_KEY` opens with a negative lookahead on exactly `key` and `defaultValue`, then `default` or a BCP-47 shape, and the emitted map type declares both members as `never`. So no spec-accepted map carries either member, every keyed reference carries one, and a map with a locale named `key` is not a map the spec accepts. It is not a text-against-name match: it reads neither the label's text nor a target. `Key` (case-differing) passes the regex and reads as a map, correctly. The keyed branch stays unreachable by contract (`NavigationEntryItem.label?: string`; zod `z.string().optional()`) and unchanged.

4. **The three resolver props and positional arguments — not a public prop change in the ruling's sense; acceptable under Clause-② `no`.** `NavigationRendererProps` keeps the three members with identical optionality and types; `resolveNavItemLabel` keeps its six positions and types (the `_objectResolver` names appear in the d.ts but are not part of the call contract). The `@deprecated` tag is documentation: it adds, removes and retypes nothing, and it is true — the old docblock promised "convention-based i18n auto-resolution", which the ruling retired, so leaving it would have been a false doc. A documented no-op prop is a contract oddity; its retirement is Q2 and a signature change, so it is right that it is not in this PR.

5. **Comment-only edits — each true at the head.** `NavigationRenderer.tsx`: the `RETIRED (9c60144b5)` note restates why the id-keyed resolvers never fired (label text against the node's `id`) — true; its "owned solely by `/meta` (rung 1)" is true of bundle translation, and the inline map is the authored label, not a translation. The `t` prop doc says a map never reaches `t` — true, `presentNavItemLabel` routes a map to the spec resolver. The action-arm comment says the map read lives in `resolveNavItemLabel`, not `resolveLabel` — true. The function docblock's three rungs match the code. `useObjectLabel.ts` (+5 −3, inside one JSDoc): "so is the guard itself" — true.

6. **The restated rows — each says what the ruling requires.** "renders a present object label equal to the machine name verbatim, resolveObjectLabel unasked": resolver uncalled, `account` shown, `Accounts` absent — the ruled pin. "renders both present dashboard labels verbatim, resolveDashboardLabel unasked": `sales_overview` (the machine name) and `Executive summary` both verbatim, resolver uncalled. "still lets an authored object label win": assertion unchanged (`Projects`, resolver uncalled), comment now says "for any spelling". The file header is restated to "the convention resolvers unasked, including a label equal to the machine name".

7. **Ablation legs — consistent with the test files as read, not re-run.** Leg A (arm restored, map read kept): the 2 sidebar VERBATIM rows, the 2 function rows and the 2 restated rows all assert uncalled resolvers and verbatim text; the third ownership row (`Projects`) and the MAP rows are untouched by the arm — 6, exactly those. Leg B (map back through `resolveLabel`): a map answers `defaultValue || key`, undefined, so the function MAP row and the sidebar MAP row fail and nothing else reads a map — 2, exactly those. The shards on the head are the gate.

8. **Fork clause — supported at `main` (`1563d3e10b`, this PR's base).** `NavigationSyncEffect` calls `syncPageCreated(appName, pageName)` and `syncDashboardCreated(appName, dashName)` with no label, and `newPageNavigationItem` writes the key only when one is passed; `buildAppSkeleton` seeds `{ id, type, objectName }`; `AppNavCanvas` births `{ id, type: 'object' }` and passes `navLabel(...)` only to the selection callback; `generatedEntryLabel` writes a plural only when it spells neither the label nor the name; `NavigationDesigner` and the wizard write "New Group / New Link" placeholders. The `label: d.name` writes are the Studio rail's object list (`setObjects`) and the package-app header, not nav entries. No objectui producer writes a machine-name label; the fork was rightly not triggered.

9. **The new pins** cover the ruling's three: verbatim under `en` and `zh-CN` (sidebar and function, with an inheriting control in the same tree proving the wiring live); the map rows (function, and sidebar with search); absent-label inheritance stays in `labelInheritsTarget-9868` (its row "an explicit label EQUAL to the machine name stays verbatim" uses echo resolvers and is green before and after), and the stage-1 pin is in the consumer set.

### ② Semver level

- The diff publishes, in `@object-ui/layout`: the behaviour of `resolveNavItemLabel` and `NavigationRenderer` (a present label verbatim; a map renders; three props inert), and one new import from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, already a dependency and already imported by `AppSchemaRenderer`; no type, member or signature changes. In `@object-ui/i18n`: a JSDoc edit, nothing published. The changeset `'@object-ui/layout': patch` matches, and `@object-ui/i18n` rightly carries none (Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Fixed Group Check and Claim Re-read are green). Its text states the visible effect and the one-line fix, and "not converted, no notice" — the ruling's own wording.
- The PR body declares Clause-② `no`, line-initial, the fixed spelling, no arm. Against the built diff and the arms in `clause2-line.mjs`: nothing widens (the spec and the renderer's `label` input accepted a map before; it now renders instead of empty, which is conformance, not a new accepted input), and nothing narrows an accept set (every prop, argument and label shape accepted before is accepted now), so neither `(widening)` nor `(narrowing)` is due. The `@deprecated` tag and the renamed positional parameters change no exported type and do not move the line. The visible change for a stored machine-name label is the ruled fix, which the ruling itself classes patch with Clause-② `no`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (viewer's locale through a new prop)** — not answerable on this card: the ruling fixed "no public prop change" and Clause-② `no`, and option A is a prop (or an argument on the exported function), Clause-② `yes`, minor. Escalation to one follow-up family card at ACCEPT is right. Q1 does not mean this PR fails the ruling (①.2).
